key: He who constantly thinketh upon Me, not thinking ever of another, of him I am easily reached, O Pârtha, of this ever-harmonised Yogî.
s: After the yogi who departs uttering Aum, Krishna turns to the devotee of unbroken remembrance; Rāmānuja (Viśiṣṭādvaita), on 8.14, reads that ease as Krishna’s own work: unable to bear parting from such a devotee, he chooses him, ripens his meditation and clears its obstacles.
src: Rāmānuja, Gītā Bhāṣya, on 8.14, A. Govindacharya’s English translation (1898), archive.org gita-bhasya

opened.edition: A. Govindacharya, Sri Bhagavad-Gita with Sri Ramanujacharya’s Visishtadvaita Commentary (1898), archive.org gita-bhasya (OCR)

evidence.words: I, on My part, would not be able to bear separation of them (My lavers) from Me; and therefore I Myself elect him (vrize). J carry to fruition the Meditation he adopts for reaching Me; / ward off for him the obstacles which may hamper him in his progress in Meditation
evidence.gloss: I for my part could not bear the separation of my lovers from me, and therefore I myself choose him; I bring to fruition the meditation he takes up to reach me; I ward off for him the obstacles that could hinder his progress in meditation. (OCR: 'lavers' = lovers, 'J' and '/' = I.)

reason: Key verse verbatim at 8.14 (verse.js ok, ref and at match). Plain sense faithful: 8.12 to 8.13 describe the yogi who goes forth reciting Aum and thinking on Krishna, and 8.14 turns to the one who thinks on him constantly; no four-word run from the key verse. Rāmānuja's own commentary on 8.14 in the Govindacharya packet explains the ease of access ('I am, again, happily accessible to him this-wise') as Krishna's doing: unable to bear separation from his lovers he elects him, carries his meditation to fruition and wards off its obstacles; his 8.15 comment on the devotees' fervid love is consistent. The reading carries these words without drift and does not rest on Besant's 'ever-harmonised'. School named; entry-check ok with no warnings.
